holidays.name: No Beard Day
holidays.description: A day for clean-shaven faces everywhere, when bearded folks are encouraged to give their chins a fresh start and see what has been hiding under all that fuzz.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that appears on many quirky holiday calendars, created as a playful counterpart to beard-growing celebrations. It has no single known founder.
holidays.funFact: In 1705, Russian Tsar Peter the Great imposed a beard tax to push his nobles toward a clean-shaven, Western European look. Those who paid received a token to prove it.

holidays.name: Chocolate Cupcake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the miniature, perfectly portioned chocolate cake. Frosting is practically mandatory, and sprinkles are encouraged.
holidays.origin: A food holiday listed on many national food-day calendars, created to honor the beloved dessert. Its exact originator is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Early cupcakes were sometimes called 'number cakes' because the recipe was easy to remember: one cup of butter, two cups of sugar, three cups of flour, and four eggs. They were also baked in individual cups, which gave them their modern name.

holidays.name: Alaska Day
holidays.description: An official state holiday in Alaska marking the formal transfer of the territory from Russia to the United States. Alaskans celebrate with parades, reenactments, and a deep appreciation for their enormous state.
holidays.origin: On October 18, 1867, the transfer ceremony took place in Sitka, Alaska. The United States had purchased the territory for $7.2 million, and the deal had been widely mocked as 'Seward's Folly.'
holidays.funFact: The purchase worked out to roughly two cents per acre. Alaska is now more than twice the size of Texas.

holidays.name: Medical Assistants Recognition Week
holidays.description: A professional recognition event celebrating the often unsung heroes who keep clinics and doctors' offices running smoothly. They take vitals, handle paperwork, and calm nervous patients.
holidays.origin: It is organized each year by the American Association of Medical Assistants to highlight the profession's contributions to healthcare. It takes place in the third full week of October, so it often overlaps with October 18.
holidays.funFact: Medical assisting is consistently listed among the fastest-growing healthcare occupations in the United States.
